doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

chapter: Photographs of the Creole Fiesta and family
title: First boat ride on the Good Neighbor, grand marshal and carriage
summary: Photographs of the February 1953 boat ride, the first Grand Marshal Mr. Girard and the carriage rides.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I was looking at the date to...
Doesn't it look like snow? But I know.
That's in that. What date is that? February 5th, 1953.

Uh, ride on Goodneighbor. That's our first ride, I think, on Goodneighbor. February, imagine, February the 5th, 1953. Famous Senegal's patio. Now, that's taken... Wait, let's see. I think on this side. See how that tree, that tree shows the, um... It was a different tree from what's out there, Paracampus. It was another tree. But anyway, it looks like snow on it. Well, it was a frosty morning, because you see everybody with their coats on, across the afternoon. This was a two o'clock boat ride on the... Goodneighbor. On the Goodneighbor. You know about that boat, of course. And these are the people, um, famous people, really, of New Orleans. This is Mrs. Um... Mrs. Um... Her husband's retired school principal. I can't see it.
Here, we've got you upside down. I've seen it before. I don't know who she's talking about.

It's Helen Thornton. Miss Thornton. And he's your friend. Yeah. He is, uh, her husband is a retired principal, not a school teacher. He's a retired principal. And here is, you know her, Mrs. What? What's her name? Druggist. Oh, yeah. Druggist man. Huh? Thornton. No, you said Mrs. Thornton, but the other lady, Alma what? What's her name? And as Mrs. Brown. A drugstore, on a drugstore uptown. And as Mrs. Benergy Brown. This is myself, and this is my daughter-in-law, and her husband. And, uh, well this is the group that, uh, that, um, took that ride on the Good Neighbor, on this state. Wasn't it a lovely group? And these are all prominent colored people. These were really all prominent colored people. And this, and we go here to this.
That's another. I think we just looked at this one. Yeah, you looked at this one? We're going the other way. Oh, we're going the other way.
Oh, yeah, we're going the other way. Uh-huh. Now, this is our first Grand Marshal. The old man next door. You met him, Mr. Girard? Yes. The old man.
Oh, it sits on the porch.
Sits on the porch next door there. Is it beautiful, isn't it, Mr. Charles Girard? First Grand Marshal.
Right at La Perouse and Johnson, I can see it. Right here.
Right across the street. Right across the street. That saddle was the most beautiful. How much he paid for that saddle? I don't know.

To rent that saddle, I think, was about $20 just to rent that saddle and that horse. And they sold the horse. He would be still our Grand Marshal, but they sold the horse. Now, this is riding in the carriage. I'm holding my head up too high. This is Miss Brown, myself, Miss Porter, and Miss Moore. We're riding in the carriage. This is, oh, Miss Hino has seen one of these. That's Miss Sattavid, Miss Hino, and Miss Porter, and myself. Oh, now, this is the group of girls I want you to see. Ah, this is taking on my front porch. You can see. This is me. And this is Sylvia, my first mademoiselle. My granddaughter. This is my other granddaughter. This is Lois. And this is one of the first mademoiselle. This is one. This is all the maids, queens, with myself, taking on a front porch. Mrs. Senegal, queens and maids, taking on a front porch. Now, let's see here. Now, this is Earl Barthe. This is Deborah's brother, Deborah Brown's brother. My little granddaughter, Lois. And this is real champagne coming out this bowl. And all they had to do was just hold the glass under here and get the champagne. See? I made it put the bottles on the bottom so they could see it with champagne. See? Can you see it?
